name: Mintage Pay for WooCommerce
author: mintagepay

sections.description:
Mintage Pay adds card, Cash App and stablecoin checkout to your WooCommerce store. Customers pay by card, Cash App, USDC or USDT. Your share goes straight to your own wallet. Mintage Pay does not hold your sale proceeds.

Built for independent online stores. We review each application.

Three ways to pay

You switch each one on or off and drag them into the order you want.

  • Pay with crypto: the customer pays in USDC or USDT from any wallet or exchange.
  • Pay by card: the customer pays by card (US cards) and you receive USDC. Shown only where Mintage Pay offers card payments for your store.
  • Pay by app: Cash App, where available.

Card and Cash App are not available everywhere. The checkout shows only the options that are open for that order.

Networks

  • USDC on Base, Polygon and Solana.
  • USDT on Polygon, Solana and TRON.

A network shows at checkout only when you have added a payout address for it in your Mintage Pay dashboard.

Get started in minutes

Install the plugin, click “Connect to Mintage Pay” and approve your store. No key to copy. Try it with test money in the free sandbox first, then apply for a live account at https://mintagepay.com/#apply

No monthly fee. Rates are set per store and shown in your dashboard.

How an order works

  1. The customer picks a Mintage Pay method at checkout.
  2. A secure payment window opens over your checkout, so the customer stays on your store.
  3. When the payment is confirmed, Mintage Pay tells your store and the order moves to Processing by itself.

Features

  • Works with the classic checkout and the Cart and Checkout blocks.
  • Compatible with High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS).
  • Signed webhooks. The plugin re-reads the invoice from the Mintage Pay API before it changes an order, so it never trusts a webhook body on its own.
  • Part payments put the order on hold with a note showing what is still owed.
  • A payment whose amount or currency does not match the order puts the order on hold, so you can check before you ship.
  • Unpaid orders are cancelled when the payment window closes, and the stock goes back.
  • An order box on the order screen with the payment status, the payments received and a Refresh link.
  • Refunds started from the order screen. You send the refund from your own wallet, and the plugin records it on the order.
  • Test mode: a sandbox key connects to the sandbox by itself, and a notice reminds you while it is saved.
  • WooCommerce Subscriptions: each renewal becomes an invoice, and Mintage Pay emails the customer the payment link.
  • USD and 56 other store currencies. Prices in another currency are converted to the USD amount the customer pays in USDC or USDT.
  • One-click automatic updates for the plugin.

Disputes and refunds

Stablecoin payments are final. Card payments follow card network rules, so disputes can happen on card orders. Refunds are your decision.

Other platforms and no-code options

Mintage Pay also has plugins and connections for other store platforms, payment links, a buy button, a REST API and signed webhooks. See https://mintagepay.com/docs/

Get help

  • Docs: https://mintagepay.com/docs/
  • Public group: https://t.me/MintagePayOfficial
  • Email: hello@mintagepay.com (we reply within one business day)

Our team will never message you first, and we never ask for seed phrases, passwords or login codes.

External services

This plugin connects to the Mintage Pay API (https://app.mintagepay.com, or https://sandbox.mintagepay.com for test keys) to take payments. It is the payment service the plugin is for, so it does not work without it.

What is sent, and when:

  • When you click “Connect to Mintage Pay” (or “Connect a test (sandbox) account”): your browser opens app.mintagepay.com (or sandbox.mintagepay.com) with this site’s address, its name, the plugin version, a random value and a code challenge (PKCE). You sign in there and approve this store. Your browser then comes back to this site with a one-time code, and the plugin sends that code and its secret to Mintage Pay to receive this store’s API key. Nothing is sent before you click.
  • When you save the settings, reconnect the webhook, or activate, deactivate or delete the plugin: your API key (in the Authorization header), this store’s webhook URL and the store name, to check the key and to add or remove the webhook endpoint.
  • When a customer chooses Mintage Pay at checkout: the order total and currency, the order number, a description (“Order #1042 from Your Store”), the thank-you and cancel page addresses, the WooCommerce order id and order key, the invoice expiry, and the customer’s billing email address. Mintage Pay emails the customer a receipt only if you turn off “Let WooCommerce send the order emails”; otherwise it writes to them only when they ask for a refund on Mintage Pay’s refund page. For an order paid by card, the email is also kept as part of the record of that card payment, in case the customer disputes the charge.
  • With WooCommerce Subscriptions: the subscription’s recurring total, billing period and the renewal order numbers, the customer’s email address and name so Mintage Pay can send them each renewal’s payment link, and the store language.
  • When an order is updated (a webhook from Mintage Pay, the thank-you page, the order screen, the “Hold stock” timer, or cancelling an order): the Mintage Pay invoice id, to read or cancel that invoice.
  • With each request the plugin makes to the Mintage Pay API: the plugin’s name and version in the user agent (for example MintagePay-WooCommerce/1.21.0), so Mintage Pay can see which version of the plugin this store runs.
  • On the checkout page, at most every 12 hours: a request for the list of networks you have turned on, to describe them under the payment method.
  • On the checkout page, for the order total (remembered for 10 minutes per total, 30 minutes for the card form’s address): the total, the currency and this store’s address, to ask Mintage Pay which ways to pay (card, apps, crypto) it offers for that total and in which US states card payments are not available.
  • In the customer’s browser, when the payment window is closed before paying: the Mintage Pay invoice id and the step the customer was on (for example “choose”), with no cookies, so Mintage Pay can count where buyers stop.
  • Card payments: the card form shown inside the checkout is Mintage Pay’s own page from app.mintagepay.com. What the customer types there goes to Mintage Pay and the providers it uses for card payments (Stripe and Privy), as described in Mintage Pay’s privacy policy, not to this store.

Mintage Pay terms of service: https://mintagepay.com/terms.html
Mintage Pay privacy policy: https://mintagepay.com/privacy.html
sections.installation:
1. Install. In WordPress go to Plugins > Add New Plugin, search for “Mintage Pay”, click Install Now, then Activate. WooCommerce must be active.

2. Try it with test money (free, no review). Create a test account at https://sandbox.mintagepay.com and add a payout address. Guide: https://mintagepay.com/docs/sandbox/

3. Connect your store. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Payments > Mintage Pay and click “Connect to Mintage Pay” (or “Connect a test (sandbox) account”). Sign in to Mintage Pay, check that the store address shown is yours, and click Approve. You come back to WordPress with the key saved, the webhook registered and the payment method switched on.

Prefer to paste a key? In the Mintage Pay dashboard go to Developers > API keys and create one, paste it in the plugin settings, tick Enable and save.

4. Go live. Apply at https://mintagepay.com/#apply. Once your account is approved, sign in at https://app.mintagepay.com, add a payout address for each network you want to be paid on, then click “Connect to Mintage Pay” again to switch from the sandbox to your live account. The plugin asks before it replaces a working key.

5. Choose your methods. Under WooCommerce > Settings > Payments, switch on “Mintage Pay: Pay by card” and “Mintage Pay: Pay with crypto” if you want them as their own methods, and drag the methods into the order you want.

6. Stay up to date. Tick “Update Mintage Pay automatically” on the settings page, or click “Enable auto-updates” next to Mintage Pay on the Plugins screen.

Full guide: https://mintagepay.com/docs/integrations/woocommerce/
sections.faq:
Do I need a Mintage Pay account?

Yes. A sandbox account for testing is free and instant at https://sandbox.mintagepay.com. A live account is by application at https://mintagepay.com/#apply. We review each application.

What can my customers pay with?

Card (US cards), Cash App, USDC or USDT. Card and Cash App are not available everywhere, and the checkout shows only the options that are open for that order. USDC works on Base, Polygon and Solana. USDT works on Polygon, Solana and TRON.

Does Mintage Pay hold my money?

No. Mintage Pay does not hold your sale proceeds. Your share goes straight to your own wallet, to the payout address you set for each network.

What does it cost?

Rates are set per store and shown in your dashboard. No monthly fee.

What about disputes and refunds?

Stablecoin payments are final. Card payments follow card network rules, so disputes can happen on card orders. Refunds are your decision. Because the money is in your own wallet, you send a refund from your wallet. Click “Refund via Mintage Pay” on the order screen, follow the “Send now” link in the order notes, and the plugin records the refund on the order and WooCommerce emails the customer.

Can I try it before I go live?

Yes. Connect a sandbox account from the plugin settings and place a test order with free test money. Nothing real moves in the sandbox.

What does “Connect to Mintage Pay” do?

It creates an API key for this store in your Mintage Pay account and saves it here, so you never copy a key by hand. You approve it on Mintage Pay’s own site, signed in to your account, and the page shows the store address that asked. Only approve it if you just clicked Connect in your own WordPress. The account owner gets an email each time a store is connected.

Why don’t I see Pay by card or Pay by app?

Card and app payments are turned on for each store, and they are not available everywhere. If your live account does not show them yet, email hello@mintagepay.com.

Which store currencies work?

US dollars and 56 other currencies. Crypto payments are in US dollar stablecoins, so a price in another currency is converted at checkout and the payment page shows both amounts.

Does it work with the block checkout and HPOS?

Yes. It works with the classic checkout, the Cart and Checkout blocks and High-Performance Order Storage.

What happens if a customer closes the payment window?

The order stays Pending payment until the payment window ends (60 minutes by default, and you can change it). Then the order is cancelled and the stock goes back. If the customer comes back to the thank-you page first, the plugin checks the payment itself and updates the order.
sections.changelog:
1.21.0

  • New: “Refund via Mintage Pay” on the order screen. It sets up the refund in Mintage Pay and adds a “Send now” link to the order notes. Once you send it from your wallet, the order, the stock and the customer’s refund email update by themselves.
  • New: a “Return my funds” page on your store for customers who paid by card.
  • Developers: a refund requested through the WooCommerce REST API also creates the refund in Mintage Pay. The API returns an error until the refund has been sent.

1.20.0

  • The “Pay by app” description now says what customers pay with: Cash App, plus Apple Pay and Google Pay where available. A description you wrote yourself is kept.

1.19.0

  • The card form fills in from the customer’s billing details, so they type less.
  • Apple Pay and Google Pay are only shown where they are available.

1.18.0

  • New: one-click “Connect to Mintage Pay”. There is no API key to copy.
  • New: a “Get started” box on the settings page, and an “Update Mintage Pay automatically” setting.
  • Fix: app icons no longer show where those apps are not offered.
  • Tested with WooCommerce 11.2.

1.17.0

  • New: “Pay with crypto” can be its own payment method at checkout, next to “Pay by card” and “Pay by app”.
  • Pay by app shows Cash App, Apple Pay and Google Pay.

Earlier versions

  • Card payments, a payment window that opens over your checkout, WooCommerce Subscriptions, 57 store currencies, payment reminder emails, an optional discount for paying in stablecoins, refunds recorded on orders, and support for the Cart and Checkout blocks.
